Barbara Curtis celebrates 100th birthday with family, village proclamation

By Miao Li
… Comments
Posted on September 28, 2026
Barbara Curtis, a resident of Atria Cutter Mill in Great Neck, celebrated her 100th birthday on Sept. 19.
Photo provided by Atria Senior Living
FacebookTwitterPrintFriendlyShare
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:31
Instaread

Barbara Curtis has a simple recipe for a happy, long life: stay calm, keep busy and treasure every moment with family. As she celebrated her 100th birthday, those words reflected a century filled with love, hard work and generations of relatives.

Curtis, a resident of Atria Cutter Mill in Great Neck, marked the milestone Saturday, Sept. 19, with a special proclamation from Mayor Ted Rosen and Deputy Mayor Pamela Markshield.

“My biggest secret to a happy life is that I’ve lived quietly and calmly while being busy enough to stay occupied,” Curtis said.

LI Press: Glen Cove Council Member looks to provide tools to educate the population on Alzheimer’s

Born in Manhattan, Curtis grew up in Greenwich Village with her parents, Louis and Emma Malatesta. Her father was a winemaker before Prohibition. She later attended Hunter College as a language major, where she met her future husband, Ernest.

Read More: Great Neck teen turns front lawn into a buzzing pollinator garden

Together, they built a life and raised eight children while Ernest ran his own electronics store for 40 years, with Barbara’s help. Their family has since grown to include 17 grandchildren and six great-grandchildren.

For Curtis, the most treasured memories are the everyday moments spent with the people she loves.

“My favorite memory is every minute I’ve spent with my children, grandchildren, and great-grandchildren,” she said.

A lifelong lover of reading, cooking and baking, Curtis continues to enjoy the simple pleasures that have shaped her life. Her 100th birthday celebrated not only a remarkable milestone but also the family bonds and quiet joys she holds dear.
